example_summary: Mr. Bhargava, an advocate, accepted a ₹ 5 lacs fee for a Supreme Court case on the condition that he would use it to create a charitable trust, which he subsequently did.
source_provision:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Diversion vs Application of Income

| Doctrine / Concept | Statutory Section | Core Legal Test / Condition | Tax Treatment / Legal Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Application of Income** | Section 4 & Section 5 | Income reaches the assessee first; subsequently utilized as per personal desire or voluntary obligation. | Fully taxable in the hands of the recipient assessee under the relevant head of income. |
| **Diversion by Overriding Title** | Section 4 | Income is diverted at the source by an overriding legal obligation before it becomes the assessee's income. | Excluded from the total income of the assessee as it never accrued to them. |


- **Professional Income Chargeability**: Fees received by an advocate or professional for services rendered directly accrue as income under Section 28 under the head Profits and Gains of Business or Profession.
- **Voluntary Trust Creation**: Creating a charitable trust out of already received professional fees represents mere application of income and does not alter its taxability.


> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Judicial Distinction**: For diversion by overriding title to apply, the obligation must attach to the source of income itself, not to the destination or application of the income after it is received.

director.justification: The case requires a classification between 'Diversion of Income' and 'Application of Income' based on whether the legal obligation existed at the source or after receipt.
director.visual_metaphor: A river fork where water is either diverted into a side canal before reaching the main gate (Diversion) or flows through the gate into a private reservoir before being pumped out (Application).
